transcript: oh boy do I have recommendations for you because it just so happens this is my favorite subset of modern musical theatre so just to start off it sounds like you're already familiar with Dave Malloy but just to recap for anyone else Dave Malloy to me is the most exciting musical theatre writer currently living obviously you've got his most famous show great comet ghost quartet you mentioned octet already you've also got three houses preludes another artist you absolutely have to be aware of is Heather Christian now unfortunately not much of her theatrical work has been recorded professionally yet I think that'll start to change in the next couple years but in the meantime I would check out this piece Prime: a Practical Breviary which is actually not on music streaming services this is a podcast episode You mentioned in the green which is by Grace McLean who is an original cast member of great comet but another collaborator of Dave Malloy’s Gelsey Bell has a piece called morning // mourning which I saw at Prototype Festival and I absolutely loved it it essentially imagines what would happen if humans suddenly disappeared from the earth and basically describes the decay of everything on earth and then basically takes us forward in time through to the end of the universe I would also check out the work of The Bengsons similar to Heather Christian they have a lot of live performances but not a lot of their work has been professionally recorded but one that has is Hundred days a couple of miscellaneous ones there's a Weightless by the Kilbanes which is kind of in the vein of Hadestown it's also based on a Greek myth you've got Futurity which is not on the main streaming platforms I don't think but it is on Sound Cloud but maybe most of all you absolutely cannot talk about this family of avant garde musical theatre composers without talking about the late great Elizabeth Swados who is in some ways mother to them all there's a recent-ish studio album called The Liz Swados Project which is like a compilation of some of her works it's absolutely gorgeous and definitively a must-listen for anyone who is a fan of this sort of indie alternative musical theatre and kinda to prove my point from a second ago a bunch of the tracks are recorded by some of the artists that I have already mentioned in this video or people who have worked with them it is a beautiful homage not just to her music but to the legacy that she left behind
